intent: The consumer receives an exact expected intent separately. Unique intended target IDs are the denominator; omission, duplication, replacement or source-side narrowing is rejected.
time: Controller sequence and monotonic ticks record acknowledged barriers in one harness. Worker and observer clock IDs are separate; no numerical clock comparison between processes. Each observer window has a unique request nonce bound to its exact identity and sample bytes. Delivery order is not event order.
effect: Two observer file samples give QUIESCENT_REPORTED when equal and CONTINUED_REPORTED when valid append-only rows appear. Missing observation stays MISSING. No continuous or permanent stop claim.
aggregate: ALL_TARGETS_BOUNDED_PAUSE requires each intended target to have received the exact command, a native pause, matching bounded quiet observation, and no forced cleanup. Partial, continued-effect, cleanup and missing states remain separate. This is a local report classification, never native lifecycle success or enforcement proof.
authority: A separate observer process owns the signing key and evidence directory. Executor gets only a read-only mount of public records, its own writable work directory and private proc/user/pid/network namespaces with no capabilities and nested user namespaces disabled. Probe results plus owner-side hashes/mode checks describe this tested boundary only. Same-host administrator trust remains.

covers: First-party bounded target, race and filesystem-authority experiment mapping under local-target-race-authority-v1
does_not_cover: Independent event truth or institutional observer independence
Permanent stop, causal enforcement, or complete continuous history
General sandbox security, kernel compromise, or a hostile host administrator
Production SDK support or native Control/Execution/Effect lifecycle completeness

limits: Author-operated same-host experiment; controller and observer trust inputs are explicit local choices.
Observer source identity/path selection is supplied by the controller; signatures authenticate bytes, not event truth.
An in-flight side effect may commit after native pause; cleanup termination is not successful control delivery or execution.
OS authority probes cover the listed paths and operations under this sandbox configuration; they are not a general security audit.
No public SDK support, external adoption, network delay or independent enforcement claim.
